Europe in 1783. Six years before the French Revolution, this map belongs to kings, emperors and a few ancient republics. Very little of it would survive the next 30 years.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ In September 1783 the Peace of Paris ended the American Revolutionary War. Britain recognised US independence. In parallel treaties France gained Tobago and Senegal, and Spain recovered Minorca and the Floridas, but not Gibraltar.
2/ France was on the winning side, but the war drained it. Its borrowing used up its credit, and many historians tie the financial crises of the 1780s to the revolution that erupted in 1789.

3/ Look east. The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth here is already smaller than before: Russia, Prussia and Austria took their first slices in 1772. Two more partitions followed, and by 1795 the state had vanished.
4/ Also in 1783, on 19 April, Russia formally annexed the Crimean Khanate. Prince Potemkin pushed Catherine the Great to do it, and it gave Russia a firm hold on the Black Sea.
5/ Up north, Denmark-Norway still ruled Iceland, and Sweden still held Finland. Sweden lost Finland to Russia in 1809, and Norway broke away from Denmark in 1814.

6/ In Italy, the Republic of Venice was in its last years after more than a thousand years of independence. Napoleon's armies overran it, and in 1797 France and Austria carved up its lands at Campo Formio.
Which state on this map looks most doomed to you in 1783? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
